issues.description: Fast-path regex /\dm?s/i may skip legitimate time values like unitless 0 or miss edge cases worth verifying.
issues.detail: CSS allows unitless 0 for time properties (e.g., transition-duration: 0), which the regex would skip since it requires a trailing s. Other edge cases (scientific notation, var(), calc()) should be confirmed against existing tests to ensure no behavior change in what previously triggered violations.

issues.description: Regex can false-positive on incidental digit+s substrings in non-time values, weakening the perf gain.
issues.detail: Values like content strings, url() paths, or identifiers containing patterns like '1s' or '1ms' will pass the fast check and fall through to full parsing. Correctness is preserved (parser still validates), but the optimization's effectiveness is reduced. A word-boundary anchor (e.g., /\d(?:ms|s)\b/i) would tighten it.

issues.description: No test added to lock in the fast-path early-return behavior.
issues.detail: The PR is a pure perf optimization but adds no regression test confirming declarations without time units short-circuit, nor that edge cases (0, uppercase MS, var(), calc(), .5s) still behave correctly. A targeted unit test would guard the optimization against future regex tweaks.

issues.description: Changeset wording is terse and lacks user-facing context.
issues.detail: 'Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance' doesn't explain the nature of the fix (early bailout for declarations without time units) or distinguish a perf change from a bug fix. A one-line clarification would help downstream readers of the changelog.

issues.description: Regex constant name HAS_TIME is misleading for a heuristic pre-filter.
issues.detail: The name suggests definitive detection, but the regex is a fast-path heuristic that can match non-time substrings. A name like MAYBE_HAS_TIME or a brief comment noting it's an optimization pre-filter would prevent future readers from treating it as authoritative.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-targeted performance optimization that adds a cheap regex pre-check to skip expensive valueParser calls for declarations without time-like substrings. Correctness is largely preserved since false positives still hit the slow path, but there is a real concern that unitless 0 (legal in CSS time properties) may now be skipped — worth verifying. The regex could be tightened with word boundaries to improve fast-path effectiveness, and no regression test was added to lock in the behavior. Overall safe to merge after addressing the unitless-0 case and adding a test.
